notes: kb/Work PB5076 owns the fix. Implemented at 85: every execution path of §1985:IX.4.5.4 GR10. Not implemented: item c's requirement that a USE procedure exist ("If the AT END phrase is not specified, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1, and that procedure is executed"), the general-rule statement of §1985:IX.4.5.3 SR7; KeyedIoBinder.BindRead asks nothing of the kind at any edition, so a format 1 READ with neither the phrase nor a covering USE procedure compiles and, at the at end condition, continues in silence with the next statement (the 2023 result). What conforms: IndexedConnector.ReadSequential answers status 10 when the selection finds no next record, and FileConnector.SequentialReadGuard answers 10 for an optional input file that is not present (item a); KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead stores the status, then calls EmitUseHook with atEndHandled set when the statement has an AT END phrase, so the __IoCheck that EmitUseMachinery emits returns without running a declarative for the at end class (IoStatusClass.AtEnd), and the AT END statements then run, the NOT AT END arm being the success branch only (item b: "Any USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is not executed" and "the NOT AT END phrase, if specified, is ignored"); with no AT END phrase the same hook runs the file-name or open-mode USE procedure and control falls to the statement after the READ (item c's execution). Probed at --std 85: an absent optional file and an exhausted file both give 10; AT END runs and the USE procedure does not; a GO TO in the AT END statements leaves the READ; without the phrase the USE procedure runs once and the next statement follows; with no FILE STATUS item the same. The witness runs items b and c on an indexed file in sequential access.

next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993; the C282 and C283 flags) reworded b and c: the USE procedure is now the one 'associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1', and b spells out that after imperative-statement-1 'control is transferred to the end of the READ statement and the NOT AT END phrase, if specified, is ignored'. It kept the requirement that differs from 2023. 1985 c: 'If the AT END phrase is not specified, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1, and that procedure is executed' (§1985:IX.4.5.4 GR10), with 'The INVALID KEY phrase or the AT END phrase must be specified if no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is specified for file-name-1' (§1985:IX.4.5.3 SR7). 2023 d): 'any applicable at end exception processing statements are executed. If there are no applicable at end exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the READ statement' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24); 14.9.30.3 has no such syntax rule, so a READ with neither AT END nor a USE procedure, which 1985 refuses, is accepted. GR24 a) also adds 'if enabled, the EC-I-O-AT-END exception condition is set to exist' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24). The rest is carried: the trigger and status ('an optional input file is not present or that no next or previous logical record exists, the I-O status value associated with file-name-1 is set to '10', the at end condition exists', §2023:14.9.30.4 GR21; §2023:9.1.13.4 GR1), AT END taking precedence over the USE procedure (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24c; §2023:14.9.49.4 GR6 'unless an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase takes precedence'), the USE declarative as the applicable exception processing statement (§2023:9.1.12 GR2), the return after it to 'an implicit CONTINUE statement following the input-output statement' (§2023:14.9.49.4 GR7), and 'execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful' (§2023:14.9.30.4 GR24).
